title: Short: "Mach 1 isn't one speed"

lines.text: Let go of a probe, and race it against the speed of sound.
At the ground, sound moves at about three hundred and forty metres a second.
Climb to twenty kilometres, and it's down to about two hundred and ninety-five. That's one thousand and sixty-two kilometres an hour.
So Mach one is not a fixed speed. It slides as you fall.
Baumgartner's top speed was one thousand, three hundred and fifty-seven point six kilometres an hour. That's Mach one point two five.
Divide one by the other, and the local speed of sound comes out near one thousand and eighty-six kilometres an hour.
That isn't the number at the ground, and it isn't the number at twenty kilometres.
lines.cue: caption: NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO

lines.text: So a fall through the sky passes a different sound barrier at every height.
lines.cue: caption: A NEW BARRIER EVERY HEIGHT

lines.text: So what decides how fast sound travels up there? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
